extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting papers to ACL Rolling Review (ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation/production standards for submitting long or short papers to ACL Rolling Review, including formatting, ethics, anonymity, originality, resubmission, and reviewing obligations. Covers what will cause desk rejection and how reviews/commitments work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR invites submission of long and short papers on substantial, original, and unpublished research in all aspects of Computational Linguistics and Natural Language Processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All topics in CL/NLP are welcome; at submission authors must select a topic area to assist with AC and reviewer matching (list of areas provided). ARR welcomes interdisciplinary contributions that make a substantive contribution to computational processing of language; rule-of-thumb: references should include a substantial proportion of papers from the target community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution types (allowed/recognized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may indicate one or more contribution types their submission makes (e.g., approaches to low-resource settings, data resources, model analysis & interpretability, publicly available software, reproduction study, surveys, theory, NLP engineering experiment, position papers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both positive and negative experimental results are welcome but must justify interest/importance to the program committee. Surveys should go beyond literature reviews. Short papers are appropriate for small, focused contributions like (non-)reproduction reports, negative results, opinion pieces, or application nuggets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long paper length and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Long papers must describe substantial, original, completed and unpublished work and may consist of up to eight (8) pages of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlimited extra space after the conclusion for a required 'Limitations' section and an optional 'Ethical considerations' section is allowed, plus unlimited pages of references. Submissions that exceed the length requirements, or are missing a limitations section, will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short paper length and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Short papers must describe original and unpublished work with a small, focused contribution and may consist of up to four (4) pages of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlimited extra space after the conclusion for a required 'Limitations' section and an optional 'Ethical considerations' section is allowed, plus unlimited pages of references. A short paper is not a shortened long paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations section (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to discuss the limitations of their work in a dedicated section titled 'Limitations' placed at the end of the paper, before the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section does not count toward the page limit. It must not introduce new methods, analysis, or results; misuse (introducing substantive new content) may lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and overlap rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted papers must describe original, completed and unpublished work. There can be no overlap in stated contributions; re-use of text from other publications limited per publication ethics (no more than 10% total tokens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR follows ICML in discouraging 'thinly sliced contributions': concurrently submitted related papers with overlapping authors must cite each other and discuss differences in related work; anonymized versions should be uploaded as supplementary material. Papers violating originality requirements may be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way anonymized review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be anonymized: do not include authors' names/affiliations or self-references that reveal identity; supplementary materials (including links) must also be anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrasing like 'We previously showed (Smith, 1991)'; use neutral citations. Links to file hosting services that can track downloads (e.g., Dropbox) are not allowed. Violations will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint and citation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning Feb 15, 2024 ARR allows posting/discussing non-anonymous preprints while under review, but new policy incentivizes anonymous submissions via awards and priority for borderline papers; authors select preprint status on submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors choose the 'binding' non-preprint option they commit to not preprinting until after the review cycle under penalty of desk rejection. Papers appearing <3 months before the deadline are considered contemporaneous; authors are not obliged to make detailed comparisons requiring extra experiments for such contemporaneous work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Author list should include all and only individuals who made substantial contributions. Each author listed will be notified of submissions and reviews. No changes to the author list are allowed after submission (with additional rules for resubmissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resubmitting, author additions must be justified and removals are typically not allowed except in rare circumstances; changes should be motivated per ACL authorship criteria and described in 'Justification for author changes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and comparison expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to cite all refereed publications relevant to their submission but may be excused for not knowing recent unpublished work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a preprint has been superseded by a refereed publication, cite the refereed publication in addition to or instead of the preprint. For contemporaneous works (<3 months), detailed experimental comparisons are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submission / dual submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR precludes multiple submissions: papers under review at another journal or conference at the time of submission (or during ARR review) will not be considered. Papers overlapping significantly with published/submitted work elsewhere will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment process is treated as being under review for a conference (cannot both be under ARR review and be committed to a conference). Violations (ARR+other venue, ARR+ARR, etc.) will result in desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy (requirements for resubmitting)
rubrics_metrics.description: When resubmitting, authors must provide a link to the previous submission and a summary of changes and revisions in response to prior reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide point-by-point responses to reviewer weaknesses/suggestions, motivate any author changes, and indicate locations of revisions. Resubmissions must be modified versions addressing reviewer feedback; completely new papers masquerading as resubmissions or ignoring feedback may be desk rejected. Papers with very low prior evaluation (meta-review score 1) may need wholesale revision and may be desk rejected if resubmitted too soon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may withdraw at any time, but a submission withdrawn more than 48 hours after the deadline may not be resubmitted until the second subsequent ARR cycle. Once a submission receives the ARR meta-review it is no longer under review and can be submitted/committed elsewhere without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a paper has received even one review at ARR, it cannot simply be withdrawn and submitted again as a 'new' paper. If intending to resubmit to ARR, do not withdraw the previous version; instead follow resubmission policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics policy and responsible NLP checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to honour the ACL Code of Ethics and are encouraged to include a section on ethical impact and broader impacts; authors must complete the Responsible NLP Checklist as part of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Ethical considerations' section is optional and does not count toward the page limit if placed at the end. Incorrect, incomplete, or misleading checklist information can result in desk rejection. Papers flagged for ethical concerns will be reviewed by the Ethics Advisory Committee; ARR reserves the right to reject papers on ethical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI writing/coding assistance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools do not qualify for authorship; their use must be disclosed in the Responsible NLP Checklist and details included in Acknowledgements (and README for code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized appropriate uses include: (a) assistance purely with language (paraphrasing/polishing), (b) short-form input assistance (predictive keyboards), (c) literature search, (d) low-novelty text (must be disclosed and checked, cite sources), (e) new ideas (must be developed and literature-checked), (f) new ideas + new text (AI cannot be co-author). All authors are responsible for correctness; submissions attempting to manipulate machine 'readers' (prompt injections) may be desk rejected. Reviewers misusing generative models may be sanctioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reviewer/author reviewing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting to ARR comes with a reviewing requirement: starting May 2025 all authors are expected to contribute to the review process unless an exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet reviewing obligations (unless exempt) may lead to desk rejection or ineligibility to submit/commit in subsequent ARR cycles. All authors must complete an author registration form within 48 hours after submission deadline and maintain an updated OpenReview profile. Qualified reviewers are considered those with at least two short/long papers in main ACL events or Findings plus at least one more paper in ACL Anthology or a major ML/AI venue (list provided). Reviewers must follow ARR reviewer guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and style/template compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must use the official ACL style template and follow *ACL paper formatting guidelines (paper size, margin width, font size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may not modify style files or use templates designed for other conferences. Submissions that do not conform to required styles will be rejected without review. All text should be addressed exclusively to human readers; submissions with prompt injections intended to manipulate generative tools will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection causes and enforcement timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers can be desk-rejected for format and anonymity violations, dual submissions, self-plagiarism, incorrect/incomplete/misleading Responsible NLP Checklist, resubmission-policy violations, and other breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting Dec 2024 ARR enforces desk rejections for incorrect Responsible NLP checklist filings and resubmission violations. Starting July 2025 appendices not following double-column format (except approved exceptions) will also be desk rejected. Desk rejections can occur at any time in the review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials policy (appendices, software, data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials (appendices, software, data) are encouraged to improve reproducibility but are optional and not required to be considered by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appendices/software/data are essential for assessing novelty or technical correctness they should be part of the main paper rather than appendices. Including essential material only in appendices may be seen as attempting to circumvent page limits and can lead to desk rejection. Appendices should come after references and do not count toward the page limit. Software should be submitted as a single .tgz or .zip and data as a separate .tgz or .zip. Supplementary materials must be fully anonymized; links to cloud services that track downloads (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox) are unacceptable. If software is provided via an online repository it should be anonymized (e.g., Anonymous GitHub).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices should follow the official double-column format and come after the references in the submitted PDF; they do not count towards the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting July 2025 appendices not following the double-column format (except approved exceptions) will be desk rejected. Check ACLPUB guidelines for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission administrative fields and metadata editing window
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata fields—including the Responsible Checklist—will remain editable for 48 hours after each submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After each submission deadline, all authors must complete the author registration form within 48 hours. Ensure co-authors are aware of reviewing obligations and registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer/review form & AC meta-review forms availability
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR provides current versions of the review form and the AC meta-review form; these forms are re-assessed and updated periodically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewers must familiarize themselves with the latest version of the ARR reviewer guidelines and perform reviews in line with ARR requirements. Authors can consult the provided forms to understand evaluation criteria and meta-review expectations.
